transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Good morning, team, and thank you for coming in early. This is our final briefing before the festival opens on Friday. I'll go through the safety plan, and then there'll be time for questions.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: First, numbers. We're expecting twelve thousand visitors on Saturday, which is our busiest day, and about eight thousand on Friday and Sunday. That's higher than last year, when we had nine thousand at the peak, so we've changed the layout. The main stage has moved from the north field to the south field, which has more space and two separate exits. The north field will now be used for camping and the family area.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Second, entry. All visitors will pass through security at the main gate. Bags will be checked, and glass bottles and large umbrellas aren't allowed. Last year, queues at the gate were a problem, with some people waiting nearly an hour. To avoid this, we've opened four extra lanes and introduced a fast lane for people with only a small bag. Staff at the gate should explain clearly why items are prohibited, because visitors are usually cooperative if they understand the reason.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Third, weather. The forecast for Saturday shows a chance of heavy rain in the afternoon, followed by clearing in the evening. If there's lightning within ten miles, the main stage will stop immediately, and visitors will be asked to leave the open field and shelter in the marquees or their cars. Our weather service will text me every thirty minutes. Please don't rely on rumours: only I can give the instruction to stop a performance.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Fourth, medical support. There'll be two first-aid posts, one near the main stage and the other at the campsite, with a doctor and three paramedics on site at all times. An ambulance will wait at the back gate, and the access road must be kept clear. This means that no vehicles are to park on the verge, not even staff vehicles. If you see a car blocking the road, please report it on the radio, even if it belongs to a colleague.

transcript.speaker: S1
transcript.text: Finally, communication. Every supervisor will carry a radio, tuned to channel three for general matters, and channel one for emergencies only. If you hear the word Red on channel one, stop what you're doing and wait for instructions. We'll practise this at three o'clock this afternoon. Any questions?
